name: Malapert A
geologicalDescription: Satellite crater adjacent to Mons Malapert, 300 km from lunar South Pole. Ancient anorthositic highlands with long duration solar visibility on high ridges.
scientificSignificance: Proving ground for South Pole precision landing, plume-surface interaction, and local navigation beacons.
orbiterVerificationSource: NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC) Image M1463385732R

name: Sinus Viscositatis
geologicalDescription: Basaltic mare plain bordering the Gruithuisen Domes silicic volcanic province in northern Oceanus Procellarum.
scientificSignificance: Investigation of mare volcanism and proximity to high-silica volcanic mounds.

name: Mare Crisium
geologicalDescription: Distinct circular basaltic mare basin created by a major pre-Nectarian impact, filled with flood basalts.
scientificSignificance: Clean baseline for mantle heat flow probing, Earth magnetosphere X-ray imaging, and regolith adherence testing.

name: Mons Mouton
geologicalDescription: Vast, flat-topped lunar mountain plateau rising high above surrounding craters near Nobile crater. Named after NASA mathematician Melba Roy Mouton.
scientificSignificance: Abundant cold traps hosting potential subsurface ice with extended sunlight windows across the plateau.

name: Shackleton Connecting Ridge
geologicalDescription: Narrow high-elevation ridge connecting Shackleton Crater to de Gerlache Crater, experiencing near-permanent sunlight on its crest while dropping into permanent shadow.
scientificSignificance: Site of the first direct 1-meter subsurface ice drilling and mass spectrometry volatile analysis.

name: Reiner Gamma
geologicalDescription: The solar system's most prominent lunar swirl—a high-albedo sinuous marking with zero topography, correlating with a strong localized magnetic field anomaly.
scientificSignificance: In-situ testing of magnetic solar wind deflection hypothesis and multi-agent swarm robotics deployment.

name: Schrödinger Basin
geologicalDescription: Enormous 312-km multi-ring impact basin within the South Pole-Aitken Basin featuring an inner peak ring and volcanic vent.
scientificSignificance: First far-side seismic observatory, probing deep moonquakes and core-mantle boundary thickness.

name: Gruithuisen Domes
geologicalDescription: Steep-sided, silica-rich volcanic mounds (Mons Gruithuisen Gamma and Delta) rising over 1,000 meters above the western basaltic mare.
scientificSignificance: Investigating how waterless, non-plate-tectonic planetary bodies can produce differentiated silicic/granitic magma.
